key_insight: MedCORE turns medical image diagnosis into explicit, criterion-based reasoning by localizing and weighting the same visual clues clinicians use, rather than predicting labels directly from pixels.
clinical_relevance: This could make AI-assisted diagnosis more interpretable and potentially safer by showing which clinical criteria and image regions supported each prediction.
method: Decomposes each diagnosis into clinician-defined criteria and localizes them to relevant image regions.
Uses multi-scale visual evidence plus a Graph Attention Network to model dependencies between criteria.
Aligns criterion features with clinical text descriptors and class prototypes, then combines them with uncertainty-aware weighting.
evidence_signal: The model was tested on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, achieving 89.2%/85.7%/96.4% AUC, 96.1%/95.2%/98.4% AUC, and 84.3%/80.2%/92.8% AUC, respectively.
watch_item: Performance gains do not by themselves guarantee clinical robustness, so the criterion localization and weighting would still need careful validation across sites, scanners, and patient populations.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
